newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm, dlr inflow, U.S.long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm, dlr inflow, U.S.long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed stronger against the dollar for the third session in a row on Tuesday due to foreign capital inflow and falling U.S. long bond rates, traders said.
Traders added the peso failed to break resistance.
"The peso flirted with the 7.80-per dollar mark, and then shied away, but foreigners stepping into a record-breaking bourse helped," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.4 and 2.2 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8010/7.8040 and 7.7960/7.8010 per dollar.
"The market was very active. Some waited for the peso to firm up before covering (dollar positions), which is why the 48-hour peso did not close at less than 7.80 per dollar," a trader said.
The leading IPC index of Mexican shares was up 1.64 percent to 3,619.93 points when the foreign exchange market closed.

Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds declined to 6.77 percent, from 6.85 percent in late trade on Monday. Traders said the fall came in response to moderate gains in core consumer inflation data announced early on Tuesday.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 0.8 of a centavo firmer at 7.7910/7.7960 per dollar.
